object_description: polygonal building volume wrapped by arcades
design_condition: The nearly plot-filling volume follows the surrounding alignments and eaves height, while its arcades, shared space, path network, and green structures mediate its scale within the sloping campus.

positive.statement: The uniform roof edge and varying-depth arcades take away the force of the volume and weave it into the surroundings.
The clear fronts are geometrically integrated into the important alignments, creating a well-proportioned shared space that also provides access.
The new building is cleverly integrated into the difficult topography, and the network of paths and green structures can strengthen the campus idea.
The interior is zoned and structured in an amazingly simple, logical, and exciting way.
The attractive two-story workshop hall with central daylight promotes exchange between disciplines and gives the institution an important symbol.
The wood-concrete hybrid system makes sense, with pragmatic materialization decisions enabling an attractive working atmosphere.
The arcade zone determines the appearance of the new school and promises a great variety.
The sustainability concept is well thought out and can become part of the overall concept.
The project combines innovative and intelligent positions into an independent, future-oriented learning workshop.

negative.statement: The courtyard at the existing technical center is not convincing and shows no creative engagement with the historical context.
The desired play areas in the eastern area are possible but are not shown.
The sloping space between the streets appears helpless and indeterminate.
Five almost equivalent entrances significantly obscure the addressing.
The external workspace areas are tempting, but functionality is not yet guaranteed at the proposed height.
The zone between the two main areas of use remains unclearly assigned and spatially unclear.
A clearer decision in favor of one architectural expression would enable greater precision.
It remains open how the exceeded total building height could be compensated for.
The large proportion of windows and lack of central building-technology areas cloud the intention of developing an intelligent building.
